title: Triton host wrappers repeat current device reads and compare the anchor with itself
observation: For N caller-owned input/state arguments and Q fresh outputs, generated Python reads device 2N+Q times, including an anchor self-comparison. Source establishes redundant synchronous metadata reads, not a measured performance gain. The related Task confirms three candidates on its original five cases but its fixed-order auxiliary burst assay does not isolate pure launch/sync cost or establish a calibrated A/A bound. No inference that every Schedule is host-bound is promoted.
proposed_change: After all existing current-call shape/dtype/CUDA/contiguity guards, bind the current anchor device once and compare each other input/state device directly in order. Share that per-call value with output allocation and supplied-output checks. Reuse the reserved launcher namespace with an entry-derived local name. Leave kernel emission, launch constants, current pointer wrappers, Triton specialization, stream handling and output lifecycle unchanged. No persistent cache or new IR surface.
promotion_disposition: Source-level redundant-work reduction only; focused ABI regression, complete Corpus/contracts, independent review and bounded same-kernel device replay pending. No device speedup, isolated Compiler causal effect or change to frozen Runs is claimed.
design_review: P1/P3 keep one existing caller ABI and one per-call device value; P2 emitted checks stay visible; P4/P5/P7 no IR/types/effects change; P6 full Corpus and caller contracts required; P8 current tensor device and runtime specialization remain authoritative.
